propositions: T11's unconditional post-rollback schema state finding generates tautological advisories in append-only and backward-compatible systems, masking genuine data-loss risks

Replace the unconditional post-rollback paragraph with a four-condition applicability rule: raise findings only when plans change interpretation of existing records, rewrite records in place, remove/narrow read paths, or perform one-way irreversible transformations

Additive backward-compatible persistence changes (new record types, optional fields, new tables/columns with defaults) must not trigger post-rollback findings, as residual data after rollback is expected in such systems
The applicability rule must remain portable across storage technologies (SQL, event stores, document databases, config formats) without naming specific technologies
